title: Boundary vanishing for an open-supported proper direct image over a qcqs base
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and an admissible commutative condensed coefficient ring $\Lambda$ of [sk-def-localizing-closure]: a finite commutative ring annihilated by a power of $\ell$, or $\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathcal O_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, where $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ is finite inside a fixed algebraic closure, with exactly the condensed-ring convention of that node. For a scheme $T$ put $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ and $D_T=D(\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_T})$, the ordinary unbounded module-object derived category [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], with the universe convention [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a quasi-compact, quasi-separated scheme, let $q:Z\to S$ and $q':Z'\to S$ be proper morphisms, and let $h:Z'\to Z$ be a proper morphism with $qh=q'$ [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Let $j:U\hookrightarrow Z$ and $j':U\hookrightarrow Z'$ be quasi-compact open immersions [def-weil-open-immersion] satisfying $hj'=j$ and $h^{-1}(j(U))=j'(U)$ as open subschemes. Let $i:B\hookrightarrow Z$ be any closed immersion with underlying image $Z\setminus j(U)$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. For every
$$K\in\operatorname{Loc}(\mathrm D_{\mathrm{ctf}}(U,\Lambda)),$$
where $\mathrm D_{\mathrm{ctf}}$ is the bounded constructible finite-Tor-amplitude subcategory and $\operatorname{Loc}$ is its ambient replete triangulated closure under small direct sums [sk-def-localizing-closure], one has
$$i^*Rh_*D(j'_!)K\simeq0\quad\text{in }D_B.$$
Here $D(j'_!)$ is exact termwise module extension by zero [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek] and $i^*$ is the exact inverse image with the pulled-back coefficient ring. Neither density of $U$ in $Z$ or $Z'$, nor a field, characteristic, Noetherian or finite-dimensional-base assumption is imposed.

proof.text: Quasi-compact open extension preserves bounded finite-constant-model constructibility and finite Tor amplitude, by the stated qc open-extension theorem. Thus J=D(j'_!) sends every input generator to D_ctf on Z'.

proof.text: Form B'=Z'×_Z B with a=fst and h_B=snd. Proper and closed permanence apply. Scheme.Pullback.range_fst gives range(a)=h⁻¹(range(i))=(range(j'))ᶜ. The complement of i is quasi-compact because it equals range(j), with quasi-compact source; Z is qcqs by properness over S.

proof.text: For JK in D_ctf, split admissibility into the six norm-topological cases and the finite-subextension-valued algebraic-closure case. Their respective closed-base-change declarations identify i*Rh*JK with R(h_B)*a*JK. Mixed restriction makes a*JK zero, so its derived direct image is zero. The canonical exact/left-derived comparison gives the stated termwise restriction.

proof.text: The boundary-functor theorem supplies triangulatedness of J and i*, triangulatedness of the hull L, and preservation of ambient sums on the hom-universe-indexed hull L. The canonical right-derived functor is triangulated, so the composite is triangulated. Apply the boundary-functor theorem with (q,f,e,c)=(q,h,j',i); the complement-compactness condition follows from range(i)=(range(j))ᶜ.

proof.text: Let P=L∩ker(i*Rh*J). It is replete, contains zero and is closed under shifts by the composite shift isomorphism. For a distinguished triangle with first and third terms in P, the image distinguished triangle has zero endpoints, hence zero middle term. Preservation of sums on L shows P is closed under hom-universe sums. The indexing-universe lemma upgrades this to all existing object-universe sums. P contains every generator by the preceding calculation. Minimality of the public localizing closure puts K in P and proves its image zero.
